assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the canonical KSOA-G1 character monograph KSOA_ASUMI_OGASAWARA.md and the canonical KSOA-G1 directed relationship study KSOA_PARTNERSHIP.md. Both are repository analysis of the seven accepted Japanese publisher EPUBs (文春文庫 V01-V07, through V07 EPI p[0151] and KSOA-V07-H-0015), and both mark themselves do_not_use_as_literary_evidence, so they are analysis, not quotation sources. Most narration is focalized through Motoya, and the items separate her acts and explanations from his readings of her. The ledger entries, deep readings, project reconstruction specification and post-V07 readiness audit that the items link were read only as method context; they are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. Motoya's monograph and capability state are not borrowed.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Asumi Ogasawara across the complete seven-novel series, V01 (the manuscript line, STATE-0002 to STATE-0004) through V07 EPI p[0151] (こいつがいるから) as endpoint, located by volume: V02 textile training, Yura repair and Satomi pressure; V03 tonal anomaly, owner consent and the stated frustration at being denied care; V04 vehicle recognition and rank correction; V05 private questions to Emiri, confrontation and apology; V06 sharp reaction to the civilian bypass and use of the correction, Mizutani interview, バディ claim; V07 restaurant line, cross-employment inquiry, briefing permission and terminal acknowledgment. The boundary limits evidence, not her knowledge; she has no access to Motoya's final private pledge or to disclosures made only to him before he reports them. Volume-level states only; the items locate few within-volume changes beyond the V06 correction and the V07 epilogue.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a located, repeated account of her investigative judgment: she notices a neglected discrepancy and makes it testable by recruiting other people's authority, consent and expertise (the V01 manuscript line; V03 tonal anomaly checked by Ichiyō and the owner; V04 vehicle recognition resourced by supervision; V06 dated witness memory; V07 bridge between grievance and action presented at the briefing). Her 勘 is grounded in trained perception (V02 textile business). Not B: her unspoken reasoning is sparse, and the items cannot say which motive decides when she pursues private friction through questioning (V05 Emiri, questions about Motoya and Sayaka) rather than professional generosity (V06 Mizutani); that is insufficiency among competing motives, not uncertainty about wording. Not D: the method account is explicit and attested in every volume.

The partnership study's directed-state table gives her stance toward Motoya for each of V01-V07, and the monograph identifies a continuity (persistent willingness to ask for more) with changing conditions: the V05-V06 witness-access cost and the V07 terminal acknowledgment. Not B: development is described as volume summaries and changing functions of address, not as a causally explained state sequence, and few within-volume changes are located. Not D: each volume carries a separately evidenced state.

Address and self-reference are analyzed as audience discrimination: あたし with Motoya against 鎌倉署の小笠原 with a witness (V01 VOICE-0001), 吉川くん as collegial support or seniority, あんた as heard by Motoya (V06), バディ as a contested claim (V06), 相方 to a civilian (V07), こいつがいるから (V07 EPI), politeness to a craftsperson beside procedural pressure (V06), and the V04 rank correction. Not B: the items locate few full utterances, give no sentence-ending or politeness-level rule, and much of her speech reaches the reader through Motoya's hearing. Not D: the shifts are analyzed for function and audience, not merely listed.

Ordinary tastes are evidenced across volumes: the family textile shop and color, a glass-workshop activity and imagined home use of a glass, familiar food and walking places, off-duty invitations and teasing (V04), epilogue celebrations (V07) and the V03 stated frustration at being treated as self-sufficient. The monograph says unobserved home routine is poorly covered. Not C: no conditional account of off-duty behavior is offered. Not E: the scenes recur across the series.

Directed, volume-located evidence with Motoya (childhood leverage and praise, V01; off-duty bids using childhood protection, V02; reliance on his field signals, V03; making room for his ability against a witness's rank assumption, V04; the V06 バディ claim; the V07 acknowledgment) and with witnesses and civilians (V02 Yura repair, Satomi pressure and Ayane's objection; V03 Maya; V05 Emiri; V06 Emiri's bypass and Mizutani; V07 Sayaka), plus superiors who grant resources (V04, V07). Not B: the items describe changes in the function of address rather than explaining what makes her repair, press or pursue private friction with a given person. Not D: conditioning is directed and analyzed per partner.

Access is restricted by focalization through Motoya. Attributable self-reports are few and located: V01 acknowledged uncertainty about the planned confrontation, V03 the account of being denied care because she seemed self-sufficient, V04 explicit concern about male dominance, and the V07 statement about her work with Motoya. The items warn that Motoya's readings have limited authority over her private thought and that the V07 scene gives little access to sustained private feeling. Not C: interior states are not analyzed beyond these self-reports. Not E: self-reports recur across several volumes.

Located conflict conduct includes repair (V02 apology to Yura), pressure on a witness with bounded discretion (V02 Satomi, Ayane's later complaint), confrontation followed by apology (V05), a sharp reaction to being bypassed followed by using the correction (V06), rivalry with Sayaka (V06), and letting Sayaka's firsthand comparison proceed during a hostile encounter (V07). Not B: the items say scene constraints differentiate these actions without stating which constraints decide. Not D: the acts are repeated, located and analyzed for cost.

Ethically loaded acts and their costs are documented: limits placed on a promise of discretion (V02), owner consent that does not resolve an earlier understanding with Maya (V03), exposure of others' grief and private lives in company (V05, judged by Motoya), and the V06 demonstration that fear of police shaped a witness's underreporting. The items analyze the costs and others' responses, not her weighing of reasons; her deliberation route is not represented. Not C: no account of how she reasons about these choices. Not E: the cases recur across V02-V07.

Play appears in brief mentions: teasing and off-duty invitation (V04), epilogue play and companionship, and the competitive V06 バディ exchange. No humor policy is analyzed. Not D: the mentions are local and unanalyzed.

Both items cover all seven novels, the complete series, with per-volume citations to ledger entries and readings. Not B: the curated analysis is two short studies, the record of her life is explicitly selective, and focalization through Motoya limits her channel. Not D: every volume carries located, dedicated analysis of her.

Affirmative located limits: the V05 Emiri interview and V06 underreporting are a specific counterexample to a consistently adaptive interviewer; her effectiveness depends on others granting authority (V04 supervision, V07 briefing, civilian records); the V07 acknowledgment is evidence about their work, not sustained private feeling; a romantic reading has limited authority over her unspoken feelings. Not B: the limits are fewer and partly interpretive, and none is framed as a tested prediction. Not D: each is located and stated as a constraint.

Evidence is located by volume and ledger anchor with an explicit endpoint (V07 EPI p[0151]); the partnership study notes that she cannot hear Motoya's final pledge. Not B: the curated items give no per-state knowledge views or freeze rules for her, and within-volume states are rarely located. Not D: volume locations and the endpoint are explicit.

conditions: Use is illustrative reconstruction in Japanese at a named volume, never attributed quotation.

Address and self-reference follow the sampled audience: あたし and 吉川くん with Motoya, 鎌倉署の小笠原 identification and courtesy with witnesses and craftspeople, explicit rank statement when a witness presumes Motoya's precedence.
Sentence-level phrasing, politeness levels and affect are underconstrained and must be marked low confidence; no intimate or sustained private dialogue.
scenario_readiness.note: The analyzed address shifts constrain who she speaks to and how she positions herself, which suffices for short illustrative exchanges with sampled partners. Not READY: few full utterances are located and no sentence-level register rule exists. Not NOT_READY: address and self-reference are analyzed across audiences and volumes.

conditions: Source-near counterfactuals only: change one item of evidence, authority or relationship from a located case and state it.
Predict the investigative move (make a discrepancy testable through others) at moderate confidence; predict witness handling (repair versus pressure) only as alternatives, not a single outcome.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A named volume state between V01 and V07, with her knowledge limited to what she has received at that point.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Motoya as her junior partner and childhood acquaintance, a witness or expert in a case, or a superior who controls resources.
setting_constraints: A Japanese prefectural police investigation in a locality comparable to the Kamakura station, with her rank as 巡査部長.
No cross-series setting or authority outside the depicted hierarchy without a stated assumption.

scenario_readiness.note: The method account supports narrow extrapolation inside a comparable investigation. Not READY: the items do not decide her witness-handling motive and give no comparison continuity. Not NOT_READY: the investigative pattern recurs in every volume.

conditions: Limited to meals, walks, local-place talk, craft interests and off-duty invitations with Motoya or familiar colleagues, adjacent to work.
Home routine, family life beyond the shop history and unfamiliar social groups require abstention.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring off-duty scenes support situated interpretation with familiar partners. Not READY: no conditional account of ordinary behavior. Not NOT_READY: the scenes recur across volumes.

The items document ethically loaded acts and their costs but not her weighing of reasons, and they show competing explanations for her witness pressure (V05 private questions, V06 bypass reaction) that the evidence does not resolve. Predicting how she deliberates would invent the missing route. Not CONDITIONAL: no located account of her reasoning narrows the prediction.

The partnership study affirmatively limits romantic interpretation: jealousy scenes, proximity and invitations exist, but the evidence has limited authority over her unspoken feelings, the final exchange is worded about their work, and how the reliance develops outside work is left open. A romance model would exceed the evidence.

conditions: Investigative decisions within the depicted station and headquarters hierarchy at a named volume: pursuing a neglected line, seeking supervisory resources, involving experts and civilian records.
Witness-handling outcomes are given as alternatives (repair, bounded pressure, private friction) with the V05-V06 counterexample stated; authority outside the hierarchy requires a stated assumption.
scenario_readiness.note: Her investigative method and its dependence on others' authority are attested in every volume. Not READY: the decisive conditions for witness handling are not established. Not NOT_READY: the professional pattern is located and repeated.

known_limits.statement: Most narration is focalized through Motoya; his readings of her have limited authority over her private thought, and her unspoken reasoning is sparse.
She is not a consistently adaptive interviewer: she used Emiri's V05 interview partly for questions about Motoya and Sayaka, and in V06 Emiri named fear of police as a reason for underreporting.

Her effectiveness depends on other officers, witnesses and experts granting, denying or extending authority (V03 owner consent, V04 supervisory resources, V07 briefing permission and civilian records).
The V07 こいつがいるから statement is direct evidence about her estimate of their work, not of sustained private feeling; extension into later conduct needs new evidence.
She has no access to Motoya's final private pledge or to information Motoya holds before he reports it.
Her home routine and life outside work-adjacent scenes are not covered.
The curated items are literary studies without trigger-response policies, probes or validation; the project's readiness audit is not curated on this subject.

assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the canonical v2.0 self-contained character monograph KSOA_ASUMI_OGASAWARA.md (reconciled on 2026-11-15 with the independent KSOA-CB1 baseline, every Japanese quotation checked against its witness line) and the canonical v1.1 relationship study KSOA_PARTNERSHIP.md. Both analyse the seven accepted Japanese publisher EPUB witnesses (V01-V07, through V07 EPI p[0151] and KSOA-V07-H-0015) and both mark themselves do_not_use_as_literary_evidence: they are analysis, not quotation sources. Outside the reader-only prologues every chapter is focalized through Motoya, so the items keep her acts, self-reports and his readings of her apart; this record does the same. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Asumi across the complete seven-novel series, V01 (May-June 2022, one month after her transfer) through the V07 epilogue (31 July-5 August, summer 2023), bound by volume. Address and relational behaviour differ by period: teasing-senior キミ and the bully card (V01-V02), Motoya's narratorial 'weak for handsome men' (V01-V03), physical familiarity (V04), あんた and open hostility to Sayaka and Emiri (V05-V06), and the return of キミ, the truce and the stated reliance (V07). Facts first disclosed late (her mother's death, the apartment, the student romance, the shop's history) are prior conditions, not development, and belong to her at every earlier state. The boundary limits evidence, not her knowledge; she has no access to Motoya's private thoughts or his final pledge, and in V07 he withholds Emiri's visit until Sayaka reveals it. Within-volume state changes are located only for the V06 freeze-out and the V07 epilogue.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives an explicit decision structure: the V02 credo (self-definition as a detective, legality as the limit, concealment by the questioned as the trigger, acts against decency accepted), kept limits (no perjury, no publication, no gifts), a weak limit (promised discretion, used later in V03, V05 and V06), and the capacity-versus-willingness finding that her deceptions are chosen under the credo. The conditional profile R1-R15 states triggers, inhibitors, counterexamples and abstentions, and predicts her mistakes (dislike-driven suspicion, blurting before senior officers, breached confidences). Not A: every motive is inference because her thought is never narrated, and the monograph leaves three person-level readings standing (confident professional, unprotected core, series convention). Not C: within investigative and partnership conduct the account says what changes her response (obstruction or yielding, a blocked channel, hierarchy, audience); the person-level indeterminacy decides private and romantic choices, which this record leaves outside its use.

Both items give volume-located states: the monograph's V01-V07 development entries and stable-versus-changing table, with late revelation kept apart from development, and the partnership study's directed state table for each volume. Not B: the monograph says repeatedly that the cause of each change is not shown and may be situation, narrative emphasis or Motoya's attention, so the sequence is described, not explained. Not D: each volume carries a separately evidenced state, with address counts by volume.

Japanese register is analysed as audience discrimination with diagnostic lines: あたし to Motoya against わたし to witnesses and superiors on the same day, わたくし for formal calls and humble apology (V01-V04); address to Motoya counted by volume (キミ 11/10/5/1/0/0/2, あんた concentrated in V05-V06, 元哉くん rare, bare 吉川 as the in-group form to outsiders); a register-by-audience table (ordinary and angry with Motoya, ordinary and high-status witnesses, the V01-V03 sugary register, suspects under pressure, phone, juniors, drunk); and recurring formulas (the summons as 枕詞, 決まり！, 仕方ないじゃん). Not A: the meaning of the address shifts is marked tentative on small samples, and voice quality reaches the reader only as Motoya's descriptors. Not C: the forms are tied to recipient, function and period with stated exceptions.

Ordinary conduct recurs and is separated from single choices: she chooses the eating place in every volume, guides Kamakura and lectures on its history, drinks coffee in five volumes and wine, never drinks on duty, drinks heavily at six of seven case-end celebrations, and has stated interests in colour, kimono, glass and jewellery (R8, R15). Not B: home life is known only from furnishings and a hypothetical about drinking alone, and only one food order repeats. Not D: the recurrent patterns carry conditions (time pressure, duty) in the profile.

Directed conduct is analysed per partner and per period: toward Motoya (leading, teasing and coercion, enacted reliance and six debriefs from V04, rationed praise, care, V04 physical familiarity, the V05 quarrel, the V06 freeze-out over the bypass, the V07 demand over his concealment), with the partnership study's directed state table on both sides; superiors by name (Nikaidō, Yoshida, Satake, Masaki, Watanabe); Sayaka and Emiri, distinguished from each other; elders, high-status witnesses and craftspeople (R10); handsome men in V01-V03 only, with the Hideyuki counterexample. Not A: why she is hostile to women around Motoya has four competing readings the items do not decide, and transfer to other women is abstained (R6a). Not C: the behaviour toward each partner, its recovery and its limits (she still uses the two women as sources) is predicted under stated conditions.

The monograph's focalization rule is affirmative: no passage renders her thought, a whole-corpus search for interior constructions finds none, and Motoya's unhedged readings are classed as his view, with one admitted misreading. What remains is self-report, split sober and drunk, a few sober inner responses (near tears at a painting, lost confidence after an interview) and the drunk grievances. Not C: interior states cannot be analysed beyond those reports, and the items call every motive inference. Not E: self-reports recur across all seven volumes and are classified.

Located and conditioned: graded escalation against a gatekeeper (V04 Miyazaki), tag challenges and bluffs against liars, frontal pressure on weak suspects, gentleness once a person breaks (Shiina, Keiko), the V05 quarrel with あんた and no apology to Motoya beside a public apology to the room, the V06 freeze-out after he reported at once, recovery within hours, immediate apology when rebuked by superiors, and repair as an instrument (V02 Yura). Not A: open conflict with a superior who flatly refuses her, and an explicit prohibition, are never tested. Not C: the response family, its inhibitors and its counterexamples are specified for each conflict type.

Her positions are located and stated: lawful means only, acts against decency accepted for truth, no perjury, no publication, no gifts, honest warnings to witnesses that they may be called; promised discretion yields to the case (V03 Maya used as the instrument that elicits Ichiyō's hypothesis; V05 Enomoto's rumour framing the reveal; V06 Kasuya's sighting used at the gathering); apologies address disorder, never lies or confidences. Not B: she never deliberates in view, the text leaves the V01 Ōura and V05 Enomoto uses unjudged, and when a confidence yields is case-dependent. Not D: the rule set and its exceptions are explicit and attested in most volumes.

Teasing is analysed as the usual idiom of a senior-junior relationship over a childhood hierarchy: the summons and bully card, 'couple play' retracted, grading Motoya in a teacher's voice, mock-archaic forms, comic self-flattery accepted with えへへ, puns (ケイジ), and drunk play at celebrations. Not B: no account of when play gives way to pressure beyond the angry address of V05-V06, and the monograph itself offers series convention as one reading of the set pieces. Not D: functions and audiences of the play are analysed, not merely listed.

The complete series, every solution and the final epilogue are covered; the monograph records itself complete at the boundary, carries 55 traced claims with native locators, and was reconciled with an independent blind baseline whose acceptance review's sixteen defects are recorded as fixed. Not A: her life between about ten and twenty-seven, the headquarters posting and home life are blank in the source, and the medium supplies no interior access. Not C: the coverage gaps are the source's, stated as such, not gaps in the analysis.

Affirmative limits are recorded with locators: no false statement to a superior or court is shown; promised discretion is not a reliable inhibitor; the V01 doubt about Hideyuki proves right, so attraction is not shown to bias her judgment; the hospital fear's explanation is promised and never given; her V05 reconstruction contradicts three witnesses; the V07 credit is drunk, addressed to Sayaka and overheard with her awareness unknown; romantic intent is neither established nor excluded, and for Motoya the counterevidence is affirmative. Not A: several limits are 'never tested' rather than shown. Not C: the limits are evidenced, not inferred from silence.

Story time is dated by volume, development is separated from late revelation, address and relational behaviour are counted per volume, and the profile requires binding any use to a period (V01 and V07 Asumi differ). Not A: few within-volume changes are located beyond the V06 freeze-out and the V07 epilogue. Not C: the period conditions are explicit and evidenced.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the action first, then the register.
Bind to a volume period: キミ in V01-V03 and V07, あんた only in V05-V06 anger, the sugary register only in V01-V03.
Recipients limited to the sampled classes: Motoya, witnesses, high-status interviewees, lying suspects, superiors, juniors, the drunk celebration setting.
Never invent narrated inner monologue; no acoustic voice.
scenario_readiness.note: The register rules, address counts and diagnostic lines constrain short written-Japanese lines in the sampled relationships. Not READY: voice quality is only narrated, and the meaning of several address shifts is tentative. Not NOT_READY: self-reference and register are tied to audience and period with stated exceptions.

conditions: Predict her method (fix on an anomaly, admit no basis, make it testable by others, seek sanction, stage a disclosure) and her pressure on liars within her stated limits.
Give her use of confidences as alternatives tied to case relevance, not as a single prediction.
Abstain on which anomaly she will notice; that is case-specific.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A stated volume state: V01-V03 (teasing キミ, bully card in V01-V02) or V04-V07 (debriefs, the V05-V06 hostility pattern only where Sayaka or Emiri are present), with her knowledge limited to what she holds at that point.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Motoya as her paired partner under a Kamakura joint investigation headquarters, with witnesses, suspects, gatekeepers, craftspeople and superiors of the classes the monograph samples; a new woman around Motoya is not covered by R6a.
setting_constraints: A new criminal case in or near Kamakura investigated by the Kanagawa police, of the kind the seven cases sample.
No interview conducted under a superior's direct observation, no explicit prohibition from a superior, no physical danger beyond a single arrest.
No romantic decision and no private or home-life content beyond the located items.

scenario_readiness.note: A materially new case at a stated period is supported for her investigative method and partnership conduct at moderate confidence. Not READY: untested superior conditions and the person-level indeterminacy. Not NOT_READY: R1-R5 and R13 carry triggers, inhibitors and counterexamples across seven cases.

conditions: Settings the monograph samples: choosing and leading meals in Kamakura, guiding routes and local history, café visits, the case-end celebration with Motoya.
Predict leadership, enthusiasm and teasing; at celebrations heavy drinking and grievances, without fixing the content of a grievance or any act beyond talk.
No home routine, friends outside work or family scenes; none is shown.
scenario_readiness.note: Meals, Kamakura guiding, coffee and the case-end celebration recur with conditions. Not READY: home life and friendships are unknown. Not NOT_READY: the recurring patterns are separated from single choices.

conditions: Only her located positions: lawful means, deception of suspects accepted, no perjury, no publication, no gifts, honest warnings about testimony.
Treat promised discretion as a weak limit and give its use as alternatives.
scenario_readiness.note: Her located positions support bounded prediction. Not READY: deliberation is never shown and confidence use is case-dependent. Not NOT_READY: the credo and its kept and unkept limits are explicit.

The monograph records romantic intent toward Motoya as not established and not excluded, four competing readings of the V04-V07 sequence, a single drunk report of one past relationship, and directs that nothing further be supplied; the partnership study leaves reliance outside work open.

conditions: Police investigative work in the Kamakura frame, with Motoya, at a stated period.

Supported: interviews (soft opening, apologetic alibi formula, graded escalation, softening when the person yields), bluffs within her limits, framing gaps for superiors, staged disclosures, debriefs with Motoya.
Not supported: foreign-language interviews (she says she is hopeless at English), outcomes of a superior's flat refusal, career or rank outcomes.
scenario_readiness.note: Her best-sampled domain. Not READY: conduct under a watching superior, open defiance of an explicit prohibition and physical danger beyond one arrest are never shown, and reception of her lines varies by commander. Not NOT_READY: interview, escalation, deception, sanction-seeking and disclosure staging are located in every volume.

known_limits.statement: Her thought is never narrated; outside the prologues every chapter is focalized through Motoya, whose unhedged readings of her are his view and once admittedly wrong. Every motive in a model of her is inference.
Promised discretion does not reliably restrain her: she uses confidences in V03, V05 and V06, in V05 and V06 against their source, and her apologies address disorder, not confidences.

Her hostility to women around Motoya has four competing readings (attachment, proprietorial partnership, personality clash, drunk banter) that the items leave open; the pattern covers Sayaka and Emiri only and is not to be generalized.
Romantic intent toward Motoya is neither established nor excluded at the series end; his narrated counterevidence is affirmative.

The V07 credit, the V06 バディ claim and the grievances about being taken for strong or plain are said drunk; the sober-drunk split is a tendency, and drunk statements are not to be projected into later sober conduct.
The changes in address and relational behaviour across volumes have no shown cause; they may reflect her, the cases' social configurations or Motoya's attention.
The fear of hospitals is self-reported in V01 with an explanation deferred and never given; any link to her mother's death is speculation.
No interview under a superior's direct observation, no open defiance of an explicit prohibition and no physical danger beyond the V02 arrest is shown.
Her life between about ten and twenty-seven, the headquarters posting, friendships outside work and home routine are blank in the source.
The source is prose; voice quality exists only as Motoya's narrated descriptors.
